hypothesis: satiation (satedBite), post-kill rest (predatorRestTicks 60), parental provisioning (provisionEnabled) and juvenile dependency (juvenileDependency) each add realistic behaviour and do no harm on today's defaults (flip reflex and territory on).
prediction: each passes the no-harm test or misses it by chance on one guard. satedBite: hunters a little more numerous (energy saved), prey slightly lower; no guard worse. rest-60: fewer kills per hunter, hunters fed longer, no harm. provision: hunter juveniles survive slightly more; no harm. juvenile dependency: independent kill share lower by construction (a watch, not a guard); conversion flat. Keep rule risk: the defaults sit at 14/16 hunters alive, the line is 12/16; one or two arms may land at 11/16 by chance, which per the rule is a failure.  (Written before the runs, keepers chunk A at 636818f, floor on, 16 seeds x 200000 ticks; baseline evals/results/e133-off.json, the same default world.)
